stimulus.body: Read this source excerpt carefully: «Two asks, because restarting and clearing are separate actions.» Restarting the worker and clearing the cache are two separate actions, so there are two asks. questions.stem: With “Count the asks in a message / Count distinct actions. / Two asks in one message” settled, which choice remains consistent with the text?

options.text: One ask, because both concern the worker.
Two asks, because restarting and clearing are separate actions.
Three asks, because worker, cache, and please appear.
Zero asks, because the wording is polite.

questions.explanation: Close reading of the note yields this rule: restarting the worker and clearing the cache are two separate actions, so there are two asks. On that basis "Two asks, because restarting and clearing are separate actions" is the supported choice. Option A ("One ask, because both concern the worker") fails because it merges asks by theme; Option C ("Three asks, because worker, cache, and please appear") fails because it counts nouns as asks; Option D ("Zero asks, because the wording is polite") fails because it confuses politeness with absence.
